clue.text: Warning triangle should be deployed

indicators.note: deployed suggests the letters are spread out and set in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Advice to a broken-down motorist: put out the red warning triangle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'should be deployed' rearranges the letters of TRIANGLE; the motorist's triangle is really anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Alerting someone is giving them a caution about danger, a synonym in the participle form.

clue.text: Rodent secreted in schoolbag? Out! Immediately!

indicators.note: secreted means hidden away, so the answer lies concealed within the following words

explanation.surface: A teacher discovers a pet rodent smuggled in a pupil's bag and orders it out at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'secreted in' signals that the answer runs across schoolbAG OUT Immediately, ignoring punctuation.
explanation.definitionFit: An agouti is a burrowing South American mammal related to the guinea pig.

clue.text: Loony left of centre, perhaps

definitions.meaning: not positioned at the middle point, as a wheel off its axis might be; left of the middle is one example

explanation.surface: A political jibe dismissing someone mildly left-wing as a crank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left of centre' sounds political, but the second sense is literal: off the centre point.
explanation.definitionFit: Odd people are called eccentric, and in geometry the word means not sharing a common centre.

clue.text: Novel triangle on the Thames?

parts.note: a triangle as a group of three people, afloat on London's river, as in Jerome K. Jerome's comic book

explanation.surface: An unusual three-cornered shape seen on the Thames.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like an adjective meaning new but is a noun: a book. The 'triangle' is a trio of men rowing up the river.
explanation.definitionFit: Jerome K. Jerome's 1889 comic travel book follows three friends rowing a skiff up the river.

clue.text: City that's currently full following an exchange

indicators.note: an exchange here means two letters of the phrase swap places with each other

parts.note: currently means at present, now
full, as in rich in something, is rich

explanation.surface: A city whose people have suddenly become wealthy after a trade.
explanation.walkthrough: The exchange swaps the W and R of NOW RICH. NORWICH is a cathedral city in Norfolk, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Norwich is the county town of Norfolk in eastern England.

clue.text: Web designer enters again, back to front

indicators.note: back to front means the word for enters again is read from its end to its start

parts.note: to dip in again is to redip, so enters again gives redips

explanation.surface: A website designer re-entering data in the wrong order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Web designer' suggests someone who builds websites; it is the creature that spins webs.
explanation.definitionFit: A spider spins a web, so it is literally a designer of webs.

clue.text: 80s rock-group artist is rank, according to some

parts.note: The Police were a British rock trio famous in the late 1970s and 1980s
John Constable was an English landscape painter

explanation.surface: A jibe that a musician-painter's work stinks, in some people's view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rank' looks like the adjective meaning foul, but it is the noun: a grade in the police. 'according to some' hints that not everyone thinks of it as a rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Constable is the lowest grade of officer in British police forces, a level in the hierarchy.

clue.text: Hanging due to setback A U of one pardon, refusals B A being ignored

indicators.note: being ignored means the letters named are left out of what remains
setback here means the phrase one pardon is set backwards and read in reverse

parts.note: taken as written; that the turned run of one pardon contains the answer is a coincidence of the deletion, since refusals being ignored names the two noes to drop
two refusals, each a no

explanation.surface: A hanging set aside after a pardon was refused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'due to setback' reverses ONE PARDON to NODRAPENO; ignoring the two refusals (NO and NO) leaves the answer. The letters A, U and B, A in the clue as held are OCR debris.
explanation.definitionFit: A drape is a curtain or cloth hung over a window, a hanging in the furnishing sense.

clue.text: Connecting triangle incorrectly

indicators.note: incorrectly signals the letters of the next word are set out wrongly, in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone joining up the sides of a triangle in the wrong way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incorrectly' rearranges the letters of TRIANGLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating things means linking them or making a connection between them.

clue.text: Monk in person may see empty life that is left

indicators.note: empty means each of the two words loses its insides, keeping only first and last letters
left means the letters for that is are left out of the word life

parts.note: that is, in Latin id est, is abbreviated to i.e.

explanation.surface: A monk may find his existence hollow, the only thing left to him.
explanation.walkthrough: Monk is the setter, so 'Monk in person' is the setter himself speaking. 'empty' strips MAY and SEE to MY and SE.
explanation.definitionFit: A setter refers to himself in the first person; the reflexive pronoun is how he says 'me, personally'.

clue.text: Get round company check, almost by chance

indicators.note: round means turned about, so the abbreviation for company reverses
almost means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: to check is to curb or restrain

explanation.surface: Getting around a firm's restriction more or less by luck.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: things that occur happen, often by chance. 'Get' reads as the start of the definition but is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Events that happen by chance simply take place, without being planned.

clue.text: Morally corrupt about excellent national service

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the next piece
corrupt here means spoilt or altered, so the letters of the word are reshuffled

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written AI in crosswords

explanation.surface: A national institution accused of being morally bankrupt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Morally' in the surface is an adverb with 'corrupt'; in the wordplay it is fodder and 'corrupt' is the anagram signal. The anagram makes ROYALML.
explanation.definitionFit: The Royal Mail is the UK's state-founded postal service, serving the whole nation.

clue.text: Colour of incense in can that's easy to open

indicators.note: in means one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a can is a tin
to incense is to anger

indicators.note: to open means the opening letter of easy

explanation.surface: Incense sold in an easy-open tin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incense' looks like the perfumed noun but is the verb, to enrage.
explanation.definitionFit: Tangerine is a deep orange shade, named after the citrus fruit.

clue.text: Welsh gossip about English

indicators.note: about means the gossip word goes round the letter for English

parts.note: to gossip is to chat

explanation.surface: Tittle-tattle from Wales about the English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Welsh' looks like the nationality, but it is the verb: to welsh is to renege on a debt.
explanation.definitionFit: To welsh on a bet is to avoid paying it, a form of swindling.

clue.text: Gun, to some extent, has rook hiding in tree

indicators.note: hiding in means the letter for rook sits concealed inside the tree word

parts.note: a beech is a tree
R is the chess abbreviation for rook

explanation.surface: A gunman watches a rook hiding in a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The breech is the rear part of a gun barrel, so it is part of a gun.

clue.text: Runs away from grating romance

indicators.note: away from means the runs letter departs from the grating word

parts.note: grating, the rubbing of surfaces, is friction
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Someone flees a grating love affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'romance' is not a love affair but a made-up story.
explanation.definitionFit: A romance in the literary sense is an invented tale, imaginative literature.

clue.text: For example, Morse code prints incorrectly when first of dots goes astray

indicators.note: incorrectly means the letters of code prints are jumbled into a new order
first of means the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Morse code printouts go wrong when a dot is lost.
explanation.walkthrough: CODE PRINTS rearranged gives the answer plus D, the first of 'dots', which 'goes astray'. Morse is the fictional Oxford detective.
explanation.definitionFit: Morse is a detective in Colin Dexter's novels, holding a senior police rank.

clue.text: Changing wrong triangle

indicators.note: wrong means the letters of the next word are set in an incorrect order

explanation.surface: Someone has got a triangle wrong and is redrawing it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges the letters of TRIANGLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Altering something is modifying it, a synonym in the same participle form.

clue.text: Tasting defeat

definitions.meaning: a heavy beating, in informal speech

explanation.definitionFit: Licking is touching with the tongue, and informally a thrashing in a contest.

clue.text: Comedians still sitting on hands

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits on top of the other

parts.note: to still someone is to silence them, to gag them
hands are workers, men

explanation.surface: Comics sitting motionless on their hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'still' looks like an adverb but is the verb, to silence.
explanation.definitionFit: Gagmen are writers or performers of jokes, professional comics.

clue.text: Misuse related to a double meaning?

parts.note: a pun plays on a word's two senses
the suffix -ish means somewhat or relating to

explanation.surface: Asking whether misusing a word amounts to a play on words.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is itself pun-ish: punning on 'Misuse' and 'double meaning'.
explanation.definitionFit: To punish is to treat harshly or roughly, as in punishing an engine by abuse.

clue.text: Almost 25 quid to tour Settle and a northern city

indicators.note: to tour means to go round, so the shortened word goes round the next piece
almost means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a pony is British slang for twenty-five pounds
to settle is to come to rest

explanation.surface: A traveller pays nearly twenty-five pounds to visit Settle and a northern city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Settle' looks like the Yorkshire town but means rest. PRESTON is a city in Lancashire, northern England; quid is British slang for a pound.
explanation.definitionFit: Preston is a city in Lancashire, in the north of England.

clue.text: Gold to buy and sell following test

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
to deal is to trade, buying and selling

explanation.surface: Gold traded after an assay.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordeal is a harsh trial, historically a test of guilt.

clue.text: Spare old paintings get sent back

parts.note: ex means former, old

indicators.note: sent back means the word is reversed

parts.note: paintings are art

explanation.surface: Surplus old paintings returned to the sender.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra is a spare, something additional to what is needed.

clue.text: One may wear a jacket right by gallery

parts.note: the Tate is a London art gallery

explanation.surface: A gallery visitor dressed in a jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: The jacket is not clothing but potato skin, as in a jacket (baked) potato; tater is slang for a potato.
explanation.definitionFit: A tater, slang for a potato, can be baked whole in its skin as a jacket potato.

clue.text: Spooner's glad rags for non-regular in pub

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the first sounds of words, so the opening sounds of two words trade places

parts.note: glad rags are best clothes, best gear
glad rags are best clothes, best gear

explanation.surface: Smart clothes for a visitor to the local.
explanation.walkthrough: BEST GEAR with its first sounds swapped is said as GUEST BEER. A guest beer is one a British pub stocks for a limited time.
explanation.definitionFit: A guest beer is a temporary brew offered alongside a pub's usual ales.

clue.text: In time, dog will get tense and shy

parts.note: Rover is a traditional name for a dog
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: Given time, a dog will become nervous and timid.
explanation.definitionFit: An introvert is a reserved, inward-looking person, one who is bashful.

clue.text: Swim from mouth of estuary by south-western city

parts.note: Bath is a city in south-west England

indicators.note: the mouth of something is its opening, so the first letter of estuary

explanation.surface: Swimming from an estuary near a city in the south-west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mouth of estuary' sounds geographic but just gives E.
explanation.definitionFit: To bathe is to go swimming, as in bathing in the sea.

clue.text: Turn frame around a specific axis

indicators.note: around means the frame word goes round the axis letter

parts.note: a grate is a metal frame of bars
the y-axis is one particular axis of a graph

explanation.surface: Rotate a frame about a given axis.
explanation.definitionFit: To gyrate is to revolve or spin round.

clue.text: Whole triangle should be reconstructed

indicators.note: reconstructed means built again in another arrangement, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Instructions to rebuild a whole triangle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'should be reconstructed' rearranges TRIANGLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Integral means complete or entire, with all parts included.
